To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the asymptotically periodic points are dense in the set of nonwandering points for a chaotic mapping, and that this result is true for a large class of mappings, in particular, those having a negative Schwarzian derivative.
the set of asymptotically periodic points has zero measure for a large class of chaotic dynamical systems and that the set of points with infinite orbits has zero measure.

for maps in the class $C^{1+\alpha} $, with $f$ chaotic and with the additional assumption that the Schwarzian derivative $S f$ of f is negative, almost every point is an asymptotic periodic point of f with period p, where p is a positive integer, and the set of points that are not asymptotically periodic is a set of Lebesgue measure 0.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of chaotic maps in the sense of Li and Yorke.
the study of the dynamics of maps with a chaotic behavior, in the sense of Devaney.
the study of the long term dynamics of a chaotic mapping f.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a large class of mappings, the dynamics is asymptotically almost periodic, and that the set of points with this property has full measure.
the asymptotically periodic points are dense in the set of points that do not converge to the absorbing boundary.
the dynamics of a $C^{1+ \alpha }$ chaotic map with nonpositive Schwarz derivative is almost everywhere asymptotically periodic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a large class of mappings, the set of points whose orbits are asymptotically periodic has full Lebesgue measure.
, under some mild hypotheses, a typical point in the domain of a chaotic map is asymptotically p-periodic for some positive integer.
the set of points with nonasymptotically stable orbits is of zero measure and that the set of asymptotically stable orbits of any positive period is of zero measure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the set of asymptotically periodic points of chaotic maps is large, and that almost all points are periodic, with period bounded by some positive integer.
, in the presence of chaos, almost every point is either asymptotically periodic, or it converges to an asymptotical periodic orbit of period p, for p = 1, 2,....
the dynamics of a chaotic map can be described as a mixture of periodic and aperiodic dynamics.
